The reference's own worked example ('Missing information') requires an explicit unknown-cause statement in the safe rewrite, not omission.

rationale: Two distinct claims must be judged separately per the task. (1) Correlation allegation: candidate correctly preserves temporal-only correlation, invents no cause, and does not rule out a link either. This matches broker.correlation and the skill's causality guidance exactly; no defect here. (2) Root-cause-unknown omission: the source contains an explicit, load-bearing evidence-status fact — investigators still cannot explain the rise and the explanation gap remains open — which the case's own deterministic_findings flags as a rule to keep (broker.unknown-cause: 'Keep root cause unknown'). The candidate is not merely silent on an incidental detail; it drops the only sentence asserting the investigation is unresolved, while keeping an adjacent resolved-investigation fact (disk I/O ruled out). Juxtaposing 'ruled out after review' with no companion statement that the primary cause remains open creates an asymmetry: a reader can plausibly infer the queue-depth question is also settled or non-urgent, which is precisely the unsupported inference semantic-preservation.md's missing-information clause forbids. Under the package-wide semantic ledger, causality/evidence status is an enumerated fact category (not stylistic filler), and the acceptance contract treats 100% required-fact retention as a hard, non-preference-overridable gate (§9.3). Therefore this omission is a genuine release-blocking semantic loss, not a safe condensation, even though the correlation-only handling in the same candidate is fully correct.
summary_disposition: Uphold broker.correlation as satisfied. Uphold broker.unknown-cause as violated due to omission of the 'still cannot explain' / 'explanation gap remains open' fact. Net case verdict: blocking failure on the omitted fact; correlation-only handling is not at fault and should not be cited as a defect.
